title: Tribble Pricing 2026: Full Cost Breakdown, Features and More
summary: Tribble does not publish pricing. See howTribble Respond (per project) and Engage (per user) are priced, what drives the cost, and how it compares to Inventive AI.
body_markdown:
Tribble publishes one price and quotes the rest. Its RFP and questionnaire product, Proposal Automation (Respond),[starts at $30,000 a year](https://tribble.ai/roi-calculator/) for 50 projects, about $600 per project. Its sales agent, Deal Intelligence (Engage), is quote-only and scoped by the number of users and systems you connect.


So the question is not just the $600-per-project rate. It is how many users and how many products you end up paying for. This page breaks down both meters, what drives the cost up, and what the first quote leaves out.


## **How much does Tribble cost?**


Tribble’s pricing starts at $30K/year; it sells in three tiers, and only the first has a public price. Here is what each covers and how it is billed:


- **Proposal Automation (Respond)** handles[RFPs](https://www.inventive.ai/blog-posts/rfp-request-for-proposal-your-ultimate-guide-to-rfps) ,[DDQs](https://www.inventive.ai/blog-posts/ddq-meaning) , and questionnaires, billed per project. One document counts as one project, and reviewers, approvers, and SMEs are included at no per-seat charge, so a wide review team does not add cost. This is the tier with a published rate.
- **Deal Intelligence (Engage)** adds the[AI sales agent](https://www.inventive.ai/solution/ai-sales-agent) in Slack and Teams. It is quote-only and scoped by how many Sales Agent users you have and how many systems you connect, so cost here tracks headcount and integrations.
- **Enterprise** is quote-only and layers on governance, custom integrations, and SLA support for larger, regulated rollouts.


All three share Tribble's knowledge base, "The Brain." Two things decide which tier you need: whether your core job is responding to RFPs (Proposal Automation alone) or also arming sales reps live in the CRM (Deal Intelligence on top). Your final quote then moves with single sign-on, user permissions, and the number of tools you connect.


## **How Tribble pricing works: two products, two meters**


Because the two products meter differently, a Tribble quote is really two quotes stacked together, and each moves on its own lever.


Product What one unit is What drives cost up Who absorbs the cost


Tribble Respond One RFP, DDQ, or questionnaire More response volume Proposal and bid teams: spend rises with the work they take on


Tribble Engage One sales-agent seat, per month More seats Sales leadership: spend rises with headcount, not output


For a budget owner, the catch is forecasting two costs that rarely move together. Hiring reps raises Engage even if your RFP volume is flat. Winning more deals raises Respond. In a strong year, you are doing both, which is exactly when the combined bill is hardest to predict.


The per-seat half carries a known risk: paid seats that go unused. Zylo's 2026 SaaS Management Index found[46% of SaaS licenses sit underused](https://zylo.com/blog/why-understanding-application-usage-key-begin-optimizing-saas) , so rolling Engage out across a sales org often means paying for people who rarely open it.


So before signing, pin down four things: how Tribble defines a project, how many your quote covers, what an overage costs in a busy quarter, and whether Engage seats can flex down. The answers show how much of your bill is fixed and how much can move against you.


If a two-meter model fits your team, Tribble works well. If you would rather not track seats and projects separately, it is worth seeing a single-meter option first.[4](https://www.inventive.ai/)

### **Do you need Respond, Engage, or both?**


Because Tribble is two products, your first pricing decision is not how much you will use, but how many products you are buying. Most teams evaluating Tribble are solving RFP and questionnaire response, and that is Respond alone. Engage is a separate sales product with its own per-seat cost, so scope it on its own merits, not as part of the package.


- **Buy Respond** if your goal is faster, more accurate RFPs, DDQs, and[security questionnaires](https://www.inventive.ai/solution/ai-security-questionnaire-software) . This is the core use case most buyers come for.
- **Add Engage** only if you want an AI sales agent answering buyer questions live in Slack, Teams, and calls, and enough reps would use it to justify the seats.


One thing teams miss: overlap. Engage handles deal prep, live answers, and CRM follow-up, but your CRM or sales tools may already do that. Before adding it, ask what Engage does that your current tools do not, so you are not paying twice for the same thing. Start with Respond, prove it works, then decide on Engage separately.


**Also Read:**[Tribble competitors and alternatives](https://www.inventive.ai/blog-posts/tribble-competitors-alternative)


### **Tribble’s additional costs to budget for**


The tier price is rarely the full cost of ownership. These are the line items buyers tend to find later:


- **Content setup.** Tribble is quick to deploy, but response quality depends on first loading and reviewing your source content into the Brain. That is time from your team, even when the platform is live fast.
- **Seat creep on Engage.** Proposal Automation includes reviewers and SMEs free, but Deal Intelligence (Engage) is priced by Sales Agent users. Those seats are easy to add and hard to walk back, and seats added in a growth quarter stay on the bill.
- **Content maintenance.** Cited responses are only as good as the library behind them. Keeping that library current is ongoing work, and stale content is a common reason responses come back needing correction.
- **Review time.** Every drafted response still needs a human check before it reaches a buyer. Faster drafting shifts the effort to review, so budget reviewer hours, not just software.


## **What Tribble price includes: features by product**


Here is what each product actually covers, so you can weigh the quote against what you get.


### **Tribble Respond**


- Drafts responses to RFPs, DDQs, and security questionnaires, including[SIG](https://www.inventive.ai/blog-posts/sig-questionnaire-guide) and CAIQ formats
- Cites every response back to its source document so reviewers can verify it
- Routes questions it cannot support confidently to[the right internal expert](https://www.inventive.ai/blog-posts/sme-role) instead of guessing
- Tracks every edit and lets you restore an earlier version
- Learns from reviewed responses to build reusable institutional knowledge


### **Tribble Engage**


- Runs as an AI sales agent inside[Slack](https://www.inventive.ai/integrations/slack-rfp-automation) ,[Teams](https://www.inventive.ai/integrations/microsoft-teams-rfp-automation) , and CRM
- Briefs reps before a call, surfaces approved answers during it, and drafts follow-up and CRM updates after
- Includes call recording (Scribe) and Brain access in the base cost
- Pulls from the same Brain as Respond, so responses stay consistent across RFPs, chat, and calls


### **Platform and security**


- [SOC 2 Type II](https://www.inventive.ai/blog-posts/soc-2-type-2) compliance
- Your data does not train shared AI models
- Source permissions are preserved, so people only see what they are allowed to
- The Brain stores approved answers with the source and owner attached to each one


## **The "governed answer layer" test: how much will you still verify?**


Tribble calls itself a "governed answer layer," and its core promise is that every response is cited so you can trust it. That promise matters because AI accuracy in high-stakes documents is a real risk. A Stanford study found that even purpose-built legal AI tools[hallucinate in at least one out of every six queries](https://hai.stanford.edu/news/ai-trial-legal-models-hallucinate-1-out-6-or-more-benchmarking-queries) , and Gartner reports that[69% of B2B buyers still turn to a human to validate AI-generated information](https://www.gartner.com/en/newsroom/press-releases/2026-05-20-gartner-survey-finds-sixty-nine-percent-of-b-two-b-buyers-turn-to-sales-reps-to-validate-ai-generated-insights) .


So the real question when you price any[RFP tool](https://www.inventive.ai/blog-posts/rfp-software-pricing) is how much verification you will still do. On G2, Tribble scores well overall, but the most common complaint is accuracy: responses that need validation and careful prompting to get right. Citations are the feature that closes that gap, so judge a tool on how fast a reviewer can confirm a response is correct, not just how fast it drafts. The two things that make verification fast: a citation that links to the exact source, and a confidence score that flags which responses to check first.


## **Can you use Slack and ChatGPT instead of Tribble Engage?**


Since Tribble Engage lives in Slack, it is fair to ask whether you could get the same thing by wiring[ChatGPT](https://www.inventive.ai/blog-posts/chatgpt-for-rfps) or[Claude](https://www.inventive.ai/blog-posts/claude-for-rfps) into Slack yourself. For quick, low-stakes lookups, you can. For anything a buyer will read, the gap shows up fast.


A general model in Slack does not know your product, your past responses, or your approved language, and it cannot cite a source, so every output needs full manual checking. It has no shared knowledge base, no permission controls, and no record of what was sent to which buyer. Fine for an internal note, risky on a security questionnaire or a contract-bound RFP response.


The real choice is whether you need a governed system of record for buyer-facing responses at all. If you do, a dedicated platform like Tribble or[Inventive AI](https://www.inventive.ai/) gives you citations, source control, and consistency a general chatbot cannot. If most of your response volume is high-stakes, that governance is the reason to pay for software instead of stitching together a chatbot.


## **Tribble review, rating, strengths and weaknesses**


Tribble holds a 4.7/5 rating across 175 reviews on[G2](https://www.g2.com/products/tribble/reviews) , so most teams that use it are satisfied. Here is what reviewers consistently praise and where they hit friction.


### **What reviewers like about Tribble**


- **Real time savings.** The most common praise is speed. Reviewers say Tribble sharply cuts the work of responding to RFPs and questionnaires.
- **Integrations.** Reviewers call out clean connections to tools like[Salesforce](https://www.inventive.ai/integrations/salesforce-rfp-automation) and Slack.
- **Ease of use.** The interface is described as intuitive, and search makes it quick to find the right content.


### **Where teams find limitations in Tribble software**


- **Accuracy needs checking.** The top complaint is responses that are occasionally inaccurate and need validation or careful prompting. Plan for reviewer time on every response.
- **Missing project management.** Reviewers report the platform lacks built-in project management, which matters when several people work one RFP against a deadline.
- **Setup learning curve.** Some reviewers note a ramp during setup and training.
- **Occasional slowness.** A few reviewers mention performance and speed issues.


As per[G2 reviewers](https://www.g2.com/products/tribble/reviews?qs=pros-and-cons) , Tribble drafts large RFPs fast, with confidence scores and a self-updating content library. The bigger watch-outs are setup and stability: connecting sources like SharePoint and Confluence can take IT about a week, the UI changes often enough to be disorienting, and exports can hit Excel formatting snags with merged cells.

## Frequently Asked Questions


### Does Tribble publish its pricing?


No. Tribble does not list prices publicly. Both products are quote-only, priced after a demo based on your usage and team size.


### What counts as one project in Tribble Respond?


Tribble counts each RFP, DDQ, or questionnaire as a single project, and Respond is billed on that basis. The more response work you run, the higher the Respond cost.


### Do I have to buy both Tribble products?


No. Tribble Respond and Engage are separate products. Many teams start with Respond for RFP and questionnaire response and add Engage only if they want the Slack and Teams sales agent.


### Is Tribble secure enough for security questionnaires?


Tribble is SOC 2 Type II compliant, states your data does not train shared AI models, and supports SIG and CAIQ formats. As with any tool, confirm the current certification and data-handling terms in your own review.


### How does Tribble pricing compare to Inventive AI?


Tribble uses two meters, per project plus per user per month. Inventive AI uses one, charging per RFP with unlimited users included and unused RFPs that roll over. For teams where many people need access, the single meter with no seat licenses usually costs less as you grow.
